diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Khabar Varzeshi criticized Khodadad Azizi's behavior in the conflict with Omid Alishah in a harsh note. The note mentioned Azizi's insults and offensive language and recalled his controversial past. It also emphasized that Azizi does not recognize any limits in his language.

Ismail Baghaei, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic's Foreign Ministry, said the agreement between Iran and Oman to determine a safe transit route in the Strait of Hormuz will be registered in the International Maritime Organization in the coming days. He attributed the insecurity of the Strait of Hormuz to US actions and expressed hope that some parties would not obstruct the implementation of the Iran-Oman agreement.
Anwar Gargash, the UAE foreign policy advisor, stated that the country will not allow energy exports to be held hostage. He also mentioned that rebuilding trust with Iran may take decades.

Esmail Baghayi, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, stated that negotiations with Oman to establish a temporary safe route in the Strait of Hormuz have reached the final stage. He expressed hope that this agreement will soon be registered with the International Maritime Organization. He also called for no third-party interference in the process.

Saleh Hardani, the second captain of Esteghlal, was sidelined by the team's coach due to his behavior and summoned to the club's disciplinary committee. This decision followed a dispute between him and Yaser Asani over free kicks. Some Esteghlal managers are trying to resolve the player's issue.

Telecommunications retirees held protests in Isfahan and Sanandaj. They demanded attention to their livelihood claims and full implementation of the executive regulations. They also called for organizing supplementary insurance and payment of past years' claims.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf responded to the US Secretary of Defense's threat regarding attacks on Iranian oil tankers by warning that American oil and gas companies and their facilities in the region would be targeted. The US Secretary of Defense stated that if Iran attacks American ships, Iranian oil tankers would be destroyed.

The seventh episode of the documentary series "Death of Khamenei" titled "Khamenei and Women, Life, Freedom" will be released. This episode reviews the former Supreme Leader's reactions to the Women, Life, Freedom uprising. It will be aired on Thursday, September 10th at 20:30 Tehran time on Iran International.

A group of motorcycle couriers in Arak went on strike on Monday, 16 Shahrivar, due to low fares and high commissions. The protest took the form of a strike. Videos of the event were sent to Iran International.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, stated that the enemy has not fulfilled its financial and political commitments. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic will decide based on the real actions of the other side. His message is that every commitment must be implemented and the rights of the nation must be ensured.

Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that the armed forces have a plan to expel the United States from the West Asia region and are following it precisely. He also said that Iran does not accept any agreement or memorandum with the US and must continue on its path.

The quarterly meeting of the IAEA Board of Governors has started. The agency's director general stated there has been no progress in relations between Tehran and the agency. Germany, France, the UK, and the US are preparing a draft resolution against Tehran.

Asghar Sharafi reacted to Khodadad Azizi's behavior during the Tractor and Gol Gohar match, stating he should be disciplined. He emphasized that Azizi's actions set a bad example for youth, suggesting that swearing leads to fame. At the end of the match, a verbal altercation occurred between Azizi and Omid Alishah, leading to a complaint from Gol Gohar.

On Tuesday, 9 Shahrivar, the home of Parisa Naseri, a Bahá'í citizen living in Qaemshahr, was searched by security forces. The officers confiscated several of her personal belongings, including books, religious images, mobile phones, and a tablet. Parisa Naseri was questioned during the presence of the security forces at her home.

A citizen in a video sent to Iran International protested the increase in gasoline prices and the reduction of its quota. He said officials claim fares will not change, but everything is getting more expensive. The video criticizes the decisions of the Islamic Republic officials.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial board, called Mohsen Rezaei's statements about creating a forbidden zone in the Strait of Hormuz a series of inaccurate and concerning claims. He added that the claim of normal Iranian oil sales contradicts existing data on export declines, and talk of replacing sea routes with land routes is unrealistic. Kazemian also warned that threatening US warships could bring heavy costs for the Islamic Republic.

Soheil Arabi's lawyers have filed an appeal against the verdict issued on August 16, 2026, denying the charges of conspiracy and links to the Federation of the Anarchist Era as legally unfounded. They also reported mistreatment and torture of their client in detention and requested the return of his personal belongings. Soheil Arabi was previously sentenced to five years in prison and two years of social media ban.

Iranian security agencies have launched a Telegram group under the guise of far-right ideology to create insecurity in Israel. The goal is to recruit Israeli citizens for espionage and terrorist operations. This report was published by Channel 11 of Israeli television.

During the match between Esteghlal and Aluminium Arak on September 6, spectators chanted the name of Mehrdad Moshtaghi. Mehrdad Moshtaghi, a 27-year-old engineer and Esteghlal fan, was killed by a bullet in Arak on January 9, 2026.

Shahram Irani, the commander of the Navy, stated that surprising the enemy has disrupted the operational capability of hostile ships. He said the Navy can immobilize the enemy anywhere. The main mission is to prevent the enemy from achieving its goals, and enemy movements are monitored in real time.

Reports have emerged about broken escalators in Tehran metro, rising prices of medicines and goods, internet issues in Mazandaran, and difficult living conditions. People have reported severe inflation and shortages of specific drugs like Vectibix. Additionally, problems such as frequent internet outages and increased car repair costs have been highlighted.

Behzad Sharifipour, director of natural resources in Kurdistan, reported a shortage of protective forces in the province. Only about 80 forest rangers are active in protecting forests and pastures. These forces are also responsible for combating fires, land grabbing, and wood smuggling.

Majtaba Karabi's brother lit a candle for him in the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. Majtaba Karabi was shot on January 11, 2026, in Salsabil, Tehran, and fell into a coma. He died in the hospital on January 19.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the IAEA, stated that for about a year the agency has had no access to Iran's nuclear facilities and has not received information. This situation raises serious proliferation concerns. Grossi called for an urgent resolution of this issue.

Rafael Grossi stated that Iran must provide necessary information to the IAEA in case of significant events regarding nuclear materials. He added that this information has not yet been provided. The Cairo agreement also obliges Iran to provide such information.

Rafael Grossi stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran has not provided any information to the International Atomic Energy Agency. Iran has declared it does not intend to cooperate with the agency before a political agreement with the US. Grossi added that the situation in Iran will not normalize without interaction with the agency.

Financial Times reported that Aramco oil facilities in Jizan, Saudi Arabia, were attacked on Monday. The assessment of the damage is ongoing. One source said the recent attack was similar in scale to the attack last month.

Youssef Reji, Lebanon's foreign minister, criticized Iran's attacks on Gulf countries as an attempt to trade their security for opportunistic gains. He also blamed Hezbollah for dragging Lebanon into two consecutive wars. Reji condemned Israeli attacks on Lebanon and called negotiation the most effective way to stop the attacks.

People report that their income is no longer sufficient even for food and they cannot afford essential goods. Teachers and others with high salaries have lost the ability to buy necessary items. The continuous rise in prices has made future planning impossible.

The mother of Babak Sadeghi Mohseni lit a candle for her son in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." Babak Sadeghi Mohseni died on January 9, 2026, in Tehranpars, Tehran, from a direct gunshot. This video was recently released.

Motahareh Gune'i, a student activist, was arrested and sent to prison to serve her 15-month sentence. She was previously sentenced to 21 months in prison by the Revolutionary Court. The enforceable part of the sentence is 15 months.
After reaching a historic high, gasoline prices in Israel have decreased. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced the price reduction. This decrease was achieved by removing part of the fuel tax.

Pirooz Ghorbani, the coach of Aluminium, stated that he opposes the departure of Mohammad Khalifeh and Bahram Goodarzi in the mid-season and intends to keep these players. He said his team is built around these players and does not want to disrupt the team's good progress. Esteghlal club also announced that its position regarding Mohammad Khalifeh's transfer remains unchanged.

Ata Hosseinian said that the increase in gasoline prices directly affects many prices in the economy. He added that this increase raises transportation and distribution costs. Ultimately, these costs are passed on to the prices of essential goods.

The right-wing party Alternative for Germany secured about 44% of the votes in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, placing first. However, it did not achieve an absolute majority and cannot form a new government. Major German parties reject any coalition with this party.

Nurses and healthcare workers in Kurdistan province gathered in front of the governor's office yesterday. They protested against livelihood issues, payment delays, staff shortages, and the management of the medical university. The gathering was held to express their concerns.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that American ships in the region will have no safe place and the Islamic Republic will take tough action against enemy equipment and bases. He added that Iran's missiles have been upgraded compared to last year and have greater destructive power. Rezaei emphasized that the final outcome of these advancements will be the Americans retreating in this conflict.

Hossein Taeb, the new commander of Basij, has started a security plan aimed at eliminating Mojtaba Khamenei's rivals within the government and preventing any internal protests. This was reported by Alhurra TV network. More details are available in an interview with an Iran International reporter.
A group of retired telecommunications workers in Isfahan protested their living conditions. They chanted slogans against the IRGC. This protest was shown in a released video.

Aida Heidari, the fiancée of Abolfazl Soleimani Al-Mooti, ended her life. She was 25 years old and their wedding was scheduled for this month. This news has been confirmed by the family and Iran International sources.

Ali Mohammadi, the political deputy of the IRGC Navy, stated that safe passage through the American corridor south of the Strait of Hormuz is not possible from nightfall until morning. Vessels entering this corridor face danger after reaching the Khasab area in Oman. The Khasab port area marks the end of the safe zone for violating vessels and the start of the Islamic Republic's enforcement actions.

A member of the Iran-Pakistan Chamber of Commerce stated that trade volume between the two countries has decreased in recent months. Arash Azarmi mentioned reasons for the decline in trade and insecurity at the Iran-Pakistan borders. This was discussed in an interview with Iran International.

The wife of Akbar Hassanpour lit a candle for him by joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." Akbar Hassanpour died on the evening of January 9, 2026, in Gohardasht, Karaj, due to gunfire from government forces. This video was released by Iran International.

The US plans to propose referring Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting. Washington demands Iran immediately address non-compliance issues and allow necessary inspections. Inspectors have been unable to fully verify Iran's uranium stockpile and nuclear activities over the past 15 months.

Peyvand and Borna Naeimi, two Baha'i citizens, have been held in Kerman prison for eight and six months respectively without a clear status. Peyvand Naeimi's court session has been postponed to September 17. This information was confirmed by a source close to their families.

Ollie Millroy survived a severe crash during the GT race in China at Shanghai International Circuit. His wife reported serious injuries including broken ribs and lung damage. Luk Hartog rescued Millroy from the burning car through his efforts.

A student at Shahid Beheshti University was sentenced by the disciplinary committee to two semesters of suspension and expulsion from the university. This ruling was issued by Shahid Beheshti University. More details are provided in the full article.

A female truck driver reported the confusion of food-carrying trucks at the Iran-Pakistan border. She said that the entry of food into Pakistan has been banned and no help is provided to the drivers. The video is from Saturday, 14 Shahrivar.

Anwar Gargash, advisor to the UAE president, stated that the country is creating alternative routes to prevent the impact of the Iran war on its energy exports and trade. He announced the development of ports, pipelines, railways, and trade routes. Gargash also said that rebuilding neighboring countries' trust in Iran may take decades.

The jury of political and press courts did not find the managers of the newspapers Javan and Tose'e Irani and the news websites Mahin News and Ashkan News guilty. This decision was made in separate cases. The managers of these media outlets were acquitted.

The Belgian Football Federation announced that it will not support Gianni Infantino's candidacy in the FIFA presidential election. This decision was made due to FIFA's lack of transparency regarding the commercial case and the red card suspension of Balogan. The Belgian federation has requested that this case be included in the agenda of the next FIFA Council meeting.

Citizens have reported that with the momentary rise in prices, planning for the near future has become difficult. Inflationary pressure has reached food, transportation, essential repairs, and daily expenses. This issue was discussed in an interview with Seba Heydarkhani.

A merchant made a humorous comment about the rise in gasoline prices and goods prices in a video. He said he is happy about inflation and price increases and that others should be happy too. Otherwise, they are threatened with execution.

Donald Trump reshared a 16-day-old Wall Street Journal report on Truth Social about senior Iranian politicians calling for an end to the war. The report stated that Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf want the US to return to the Islamabad agreement.

Abolfazl Rostami and Erfan Moradi Dangi, two citizens of Qasr-e Shirin and detainees of the December 2025 protests, were each sentenced to five years in prison by the Revolutionary Court of this city.

The Aramco refinery in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, was targeted in an attack. This occurred simultaneously with Qalibaf's threat to target oil and energy facilities in the region. More details were provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Qalibaf threatened that if Iranian oil tankers are attacked, Tehran will target American oil and gas companies in the region. At the same time, the IRGC fired a medium-range missile at warships for the first time. These developments occurred following Trump's signals for an attack on Kharg Island.

An online taxi driver sent a video to Iran International reporting a sharp decrease in passengers and financial difficulties due to rising essential goods prices. He says he can no longer cover living expenses through online taxi work. This highlights the impact of inflation on online businesses.

On Sunday, September 6, intelligence agents searched the homes of three Bahá'í families in Isfahan. Personal belongings, property, and documents of these families were confiscated during the operation. Agents seized electronic devices, gold, jewelry, and other possessions.

Khoddad Azizi, the manager of Tractor team, insulted Omid Alishah after the match with Gol Gohar. This incident sparked widespread reactions in Iran's public and media space. The issue of some government-affiliated figures acting beyond the law has also been raised.

A video shows a birthday ceremony for Rasoul Ziaei held at his grave. Rasoul Ziaei was a 26-year-old athlete who was shot by suppression forces in front of the Fooladshahr courthouse on January 8, 2026, and died.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said the Islamic Republic is trying to increase the economic and political costs of the crisis for the US and its allies by escalating tensions in the region. He noted that Donald Trump's reposting of the Wall Street Journal report indicates satisfaction with the maximum pressure strategy. Trump aims to show that the pressures have brought the Islamic Republic closer to accepting Washington's demands or collapse.

Abbas Goudarzi, spokesperson of the Parliament's presidium, said that economic siege is not the goal but a tool to collapse the system. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic has many untapped cards and the era of hit-and-run tactics in military and economic fields is over. He also mentioned that if Iranian ships cannot navigate, no other ships will be able to either.

Canada's Public Security Ministry described the military threat against Persian-language journalists as state terrorism and transnational repression. A special protective network by the federal police and security agencies has been activated to protect journalists in Canada. This response followed the announcement that staff of Iran International and three other Persian media outlets were listed as military targets by the Islamic Republic.

The price of gas station cards will double from 5,000 to 10,000 tomans. This increase will affect fares, goods prices, and people's daily expenses. A program is organized to hear real stories from people about the impact of this price hike.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation issued its ruling on the clashes during the Tractor and Gol Gohar match. Khodadad Azizi, Tractor's head, was fined 2 billion tomans and banned from stadiums for 4 months. Additionally, Tractor and Gol Gohar clubs were fined financially.

Official employees of Iran's oil industry held protests on offshore platforms of Pars Oil and Gas Company and Asaluyeh. They demand the removal of salary caps, adjustment of minimum wages, and payment of financial arrears according to Article 10 of the Ministry of Oil law. These protests take place every Monday.

The US is presenting a resolution at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting to refer Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council. The resolution calls for the return of inspectors and resumption of inspections at Iran's nuclear sites. The US, UK, France, and Germany say Iran has not provided verifiable information about its enriched uranium stockpiles.

The Administrative Justice Court confirmed the four-month temporary suspension of Salah Haji-Mirzaei, a teachers' union activist in Sanandaj. The 31st appellate branch rejected his complaint and upheld the temporary suspension penalty. This ruling is related to administrative violations by the Ministry of Education.

Persepolis football team defeated Zob Ahan 2-0 in the sixth week of the Premier League and moved up to second place. Ali Alipour and Pouria Shahabadi scored for Persepolis. Mehdi Tartaar included Aston Aronov in the starting lineup, and the referee reviewed a suspicious penalty incident but the result remained unchanged.

Abdolkareem Hosseinzadeh stated that the president personally followed up on Sardar Azmoun's return to the national football team and 90% of the issues have been resolved. Hosseinzadeh called Azmoun a national asset and urged his return. Azmoun was removed from the national team after posting a photo with the ruler of Dubai.

The head of the Nursing Organization in Dezful announced that nurses' claims, including six months of work bonuses and three months of overtime, have not been paid. Additionally, some drivers of Tehran's public bus company have unpaid insurance claims. This issue has been raised by the workers and drivers of the bus company.

Kamran Hekmati, a 71-year-old dual Iranian-American Jewish citizen with cancer, was released from Evin prison. Despite his release, he remains banned from leaving the country. He is not allowed to leave Iran.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad said in the program "Cheshmandaz" that the victory of the far-right in Germany could weaken Europe and strengthen the positions of Putin, the Revolutionary Guards, and Mojtaba Khamenei. He added that this rise would expand the scope for dictators and increase concerns among migrants and political refugees.

Volker Turk, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, warned that advanced artificial intelligence could become an existential threat to humanity. He called for comprehensive action to ensure the safety and security of AI. The UN had previously called for global coordination in AI governance.

Tractor football team leads the Premier League by three points over Persepolis and has kept a clean sheet in all six past matches. Persepolis reached second place by defeating Zob Ahan, Esteghlal, and Aluminium. In the sixth week, most home teams won their matches with full points.

The commander of the Urmia border regiment announced the arrest of a citizen at one of the regiment's checkpoints. The individual is accused of having connections with an opposition group against the Islamic Republic. More details are provided in the full report.

The seventh-day ceremony of Ali Mirrezaei, a Mazandaran singer who was executed last week, was held. This ceremony has sparked a discussion about how society should deal with serious offenses and the death penalty. The large public attendance at the ceremony had a significant social impact.

At least 10 Sunni Arab citizens were arrested in Ahvaz on Friday, September 3rd, by intelligence forces. They were attending a meeting in the Mashali neighborhood and were transferred to an unknown location after arrest. The identities of three detainees have been confirmed.

Shaker Bouri, a satirist from Abadan, was sentenced by Branch 101 of the Criminal Court Two of Abadan to 13 months and 20 days of imprisonment and a fine. His charges include spreading falsehoods with intent to harm and insulting a member of parliament. The fine imposed on him is 45 million rials.

The Canadian Federal Court has ordered the government to make a final decision within 60 days on Naser Mansour Sharifloo's temporary residence visa application. His visa request had been pending for over 900 days due to security reviews. Canadian security agencies have scrutinized thousands of applications related to affiliates of the Iranian government and canceled hundreds of visas.

A video from the fruit and vegetable market in Isfahan on Monday, 16 Shahrivar, has been released. The video shows the market's sluggishness and emptiness of customers. The market's condition on this day is depicted.

Shaker Bouri, a satirist, announced that he was sentenced to 13 months and 20 days in prison due to a complaint by Mousa Ghasnafaraabadi. He said the verdict was issued in less than 48 hours. Bouri made ironic remarks about the country's problems and his imprisonment.

Shahier Shaheed Thalath said the attack on Saudi oil facilities delays reconstruction more than reducing production capacity. The Islamic Republic aims to raise oil prices above $100 to pressure the US and its allies. Global markets have largely factored these tensions into oil prices, so a sharp price spike is unlikely.

Mehdi Tartaar stated after Persepolis' victory over Zob Ahan that he changed the course of the game with the help of the team's captains. He emphasized the important role of the captains in team cohesion. Additionally, a disagreement between Esteghlal's coach and the team's second captain has become a major controversy.

A citizen complained about power outages in their area in a video sent to Iran International. They said they contacted the electricity department and were told no directive had been received to prevent outages. The citizen accused the minister of lying.

Hojjat Karimi, CEO of Tractor, explained that Khodadad Azizi's insults after the match with Gol Gohar were reactions to events during the game. He said a Gol Gohar player insulted the referee, and the referee gave Khodadad a card. He also mentioned that Omid Alishah's disrespect towards Khodadad in the locker room triggered this reaction.

Hojat Karimi, CEO of Tractor, reacted to Khodadad Azizi's insults towards Omid Alishah and the release of the audio file, saying it worsened the public mood. He also questioned the disciplinary committee's decision to ban Khodadad from stadiums. Karimi added that Shoja Khalilzadeh complained after the game against Gol Gohar about why incidents were not allowed in the stands.

The Yemeni Deputy Defense Minister announced the decision to liberate Sanaa from Houthi control. Yemeni armed forces have thwarted the Islamic Republic's plan to control the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Yemeni army jets bombed Houthi positions in Taiz.

Sergey Lavrov, Russia's foreign minister, called for the Islamic Republic of Iran to participate in a regional security system in the Persian Gulf. He said this step could be a practical move to ensure regional stability. Lavrov also described the Mecca defense agreement as a framework for collective security.

Mohammad Esfandyarpour, CEO of Gol Gohar, responded to the Tractor CEO's remarks about recording and broadcasting Khodadad Azizi's insults, stating that broadcasting these insults is not an issue. He is unaware of the altercation process between the two teams' locker rooms and said the disciplinary committee made its decision about Omid Alishah's suspension based on the match observer's report. Esfandyarpour emphasized that there is evidence showing no wrongdoing from Gol Gohar's side.

The spokesperson of Qatar's Foreign Ministry called for coordinated efforts by regional countries to gradually reduce tensions and prevent the spread of military conflict. He identified keeping the Strait of Hormuz open and reducing economic pressures on the people of the region as two urgent priorities. The US Secretary of Defense also warned that if Iranian forces target US ships, Washington will destroy Iranian oil tankers.

Meysam Mehrani said the main goal of the Houthis is to maintain their ability to pressure shipping and their strategic role for the Islamic Republic. If forced to focus on ground defense, their operational value to Tehran will decrease. The Islamic Republic must choose between increasing military support or accepting a reduced role for the Houthis, with Hezbollah remaining a higher priority.

Some fuel pumps in Iran cannot register the 10,000 toman gasoline price due to being outdated. As a temporary fix, the number 1,000 is displayed with a fixed zero next to it. This report was published by the Islamic Republic state television.

Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic have retreated after heavy clashes in several key fronts in Yemen. Yemeni government forces have taken control of two important areas in Al Bayda province. Additionally, the hills overlooking the city of Hays and the entrance to the Al-Jarahi area have been captured from the Houthis.

The Iranian mission to the IAEA called the request for unconditional implementation of safeguards meaningless. It reacted to Rafael Grossi's statements about inspectors' lack of access and demanded an end to politically influenced reporting. It also emphasized that Iran has the right to protect its national interests until attacks by the US and Israel on its nuclear facilities cease.

Satellite images show that since the reimposition of the US naval blockade in late July, ship activity at the ports of Rajaei and Khomeini has sharply declined. This reduction in activity has increased pressure on Iran's imports and exports. Copernicus images reveal significant changes in ship presence and terminal activity at these ports.

Two luxury penthouses linked to Mojtaba Khamenei's financial network have been put up for sale in a building overlooking Kensington Palace in London. The total price of these two properties is close to 36 million pounds. This issue was reported by The Sunday Times.

Sergey Ryabkov stated that the situation in Iran is the most important issue on BRICS' political agenda and a significant part of the upcoming summit will be dedicated to it. He mentioned that some BRICS members have a critical stance towards Tehran's recent actions but did not name them. The situation in the Persian Gulf is also an urgent topic, and the outcome of the negotiations is still uncertain.

Fouad Hussein, Iraq's Foreign Minister, emphasized the importance of opening dialogue channels among stakeholders to achieve peaceful solutions. He reiterated Baghdad's stance supporting countries' sovereignty and rejecting war and conflict expansion. He also stressed prioritizing dialogue and diplomatic tools to reduce tensions and achieve regional security.

Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that with America's victory in the war against the Islamic Republic, oil prices will sharply decrease. He predicted that gasoline prices would first drop to three dollars and then to less than two dollars per gallon. Trump said this change would happen quickly.

Jason Brodsky claimed that the escalation of tensions by the Houthis is coordinated with IRGC commanders in the Persian Gulf. He added that Tehran wants the Houthis to control Taiz to influence the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Majid Ibn al-Reza, the acting defense minister, claimed that the country's military forces have the ability to target American combat ships.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, called Canada's statement supporting the US economic war against Tehran complicity in lawbreaking. He said Canada cannot claim to be a promoter of peace while supporting illegal US actions. Baqaei described this behavior as a sign of strategic confusion and submission to bullying.

Ali Madanizadeh, Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance, stated that developing relations with Russia is part of the government's plans. Masoud Pezeshkian is seriously pursuing joint projects between Tehran and Moscow. Securing essential goods from the Eurasian region, especially Russia, is a government priority.

Prince Reza Pahlavi held a virtual meeting with senior representatives and senators of the Australian coalition. Senators described him as a symbol of opposition to the regime and support for democracy. The Australian coalition has invited him to visit the country.

The Iraqi embassy in Tehran announced that the crisis involving Iraqi students in Semnan province has been resolved. The students have been granted a one-month academic leave. This measure will help restore stability to the university environment.

The "Bring Our Families Home" campaign on X called on the Islamic Republic and the US government to take action for the release of Reza Valizadeh, an American citizen, from Evin Prison. The campaign described this as a small, low-cost goodwill gesture to return a son to his elderly parents. The campaign members are families of American hostages and unlawful detainees.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated in a meeting with members of the Qom Seminary Society that filtering has destroyed the Islamic Republic's security oversight. He added that the approach of sanctioning technology does not work and the internet is like a highway that should not be entirely blocked. He also mentioned that a special committee for cyberspace management was formed by order of Pezeshkian to complete the national information network plan.

Gholamreza Tajgardoon stated that the enemies have not achieved their goals and resistance has a cost but will continue. He added that people have been patient and success will be achieved. He also announced that the US will not impose new sanctions and the current situation will persist.

Rafael Grossi stated that the IAEA is unaware of the status of Iran's enriched uranium stocks. Inspectors still do not have access to Iran's nuclear facilities. These remarks were made at the IAEA Board of Governors quarterly meeting.

Security forces searched the home of Parisa Naseri, a Baha'i citizen in Qaemshahr, and confiscated her personal belongings. Iraj Shakour and Pedram Abhar, two Baha'i citizens in Tehran, were arrested after visiting the Tehran Security Prosecutor's Office and transferred to prison. A spokesperson for the Baha'i International Community explained the increasing pressure on Baha'i citizens in Iran.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated that the real cost of importing one liter of gasoline is over 70,000 tomans, and the third gasoline price of 10,000 tomans is far from the actual cost. He said imported gasoline will be gradually liberalized with price adjustments. Also, a plan to reduce fuel smuggling in three provinces was approved, but the fourth gasoline price was added without approval.

Saudi officials reported that a wave of attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia injured 73 people. The attacks targeted civilian and economic facilities in several Saudi cities. The Saudi-led coalition stated it will take all necessary operational measures to deter the Houthis.

Dave Sharma, an Australian senator, described Reza Pahlavi as an important voice in political discussions about Iran's future. He stated that Australia desires a peaceful political change in Iran. He also said that Australia does not support the current government.

Kambiz Tavana said that with the escalation of conflicts between Yemeni government forces and Houthis, the restriction of arms shipment routes from Iran, and the increase of US military presence in the region, the equations of Yemen and the Strait of Hormuz have entered a new phase. CENTCOM movements and the continued limited passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz have added to the sensitivity of the situation.

More than 150 people attacked a private dormitory of Iraqi students in Semnan, injuring several students. Semnan University denied any clashes between Iranian and foreign students. The Iraqi embassy announced that the crisis involving Iraqi students in Semnan has been resolved and they have been granted a one-month academic leave.

Three senior members of Australia's federal opposition coalition supported Reza Pahlavi as a key figure for Iran's transition to a free and democratic future. They described the Islamic Republic as a criminal and terrorist regime. They considered engagement with Reza Pahlavi an important symbol for freedom and democracy.

Prices are increasing moment by moment, making future planning impossible. Salaries have only slightly increased, reducing purchasing power. People are forced to severely economize to meet their essential needs.

Ali Nikzad, the Deputy Speaker of the Parliament, stated that American soldiers have been displaced to hotels due to their bases being targeted and are experiencing depression. He suggested that the US should withdraw from the war as soon as possible. Nikzad also emphasized that the Islamic Republic is conducting the war with precise tactics.

Heydar Baharvand, head of the league organization, stated that the last season's league has no champion and the case is closed. The league spokesperson said Esteghlal's request for the championship trophy will be reviewed by the Football Federation's board. Ali Tajernia, chairman of Esteghlal's board, emphasized they will pursue the championship trophy issue.

Jassim Mohammed Al-Budaiwi strongly condemned the Houthi attacks on civilians and facilities in southern Saudi Arabia. He described these attacks as violations of international laws and acts of terrorism. The GCC Secretary-General called for a firm stance from the international community against these attacks.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing armed Basij members stationed on the roof of a Basij base in Khomeini Shahr on the evening of Monday, September 6. The video was sent to Iran International. The exact time of the event is the evening of Monday, September 6.

Morteza Kazemian criticized the government's justification for the gasoline price increase. He said that reducing costs to citizens ignores the widespread economic pressure on most people. He also warned that the fuel price increase could trigger a chain of price hikes and intensify dissatisfaction.

The CEO of the Sports Facilities Development and Maintenance Company announced that the construction work at Azadi Stadium will be completed in October, with initial operation at full capacity in December. The renovation is underway according to an 18-month contract and is within the allowed timeframe. New requirements from the Football Federation and the Asian Confederation will not prevent the holding of matches.
Videos received by Iran International show that the streets of Rasht were flooded after rain on the evening of Monday, 16 Shahrivar.

Tractor club has protested the four-month suspension of Khodadad Azizi and is pursuing the case of conflict and insults in the match against Gol Gohar in the appeals committee. The club considers the issued ruling disproportionate and claims that the Gol Gohar player committed multiple violations. Tractor has called for proportionality between the offense and punishment based on official documents.

A video shows the deployment of special forces in Kashani Boulevard and around Sadeghiyeh in Tehran. This occurred on the evening of Monday, September 6. The source of this news is Iran International.

Ali Kazemi, the judiciary spokesperson, announced that new cases related to war accusations are being formed. The volume of seized assets in these cases is very large and requires time for investigation. Some cases have indictments issued and in some instances, verdicts have been delivered.

On Monday, 16 Shahrivar, security forces created a security atmosphere in Khorramabad by deploying machine guns, vehicles, and motorcycles throughout the city. This news is based on a video received by Iran International.

Safar Harandi stated that the social capital of the system has risen above 50% after the war. He attributed the increase in public trust to the system's ability to confront global powers. He also said that Ali Khamenei increased hope among the people through his speeches and presence.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission, stated that the Islamic Republic has the power and will to validate its threats and warned the IAEA against making regrettable decisions. He mentioned that Iran has many capacities to confront the Board of Governors and the Security Council and will use them when necessary. Azizi emphasized that Iran prioritizes its interests and is different from before the 40-day war.
A video shows cars lined up for gasoline in Shahr-e Rey. The video is from the evening of Monday, 16 Shahrivar. A fuel price increase is imminent.

Vahid Alizadeh Rezazi, a poet and translator, has been summoned to serve a 75-day prison sentence. He was previously sentenced to 75 days in prison and a three-year ban on media activities. The summons was issued by the Criminal Enforcement Branch 1 of the Tehran Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office.

Khoddad Azizi was banned from stadiums for 4 months and fined 2 billion tomans. Omid Alishah was also banned for 4 matches and fined 500 million tomans. Tractor club considered the ruling disproportionate and plans to appeal to the disciplinary committee.
